_readme: Day scenes (job dayscenes): a real ~1 minute scene per day = 10-15 s Downtown News montage (data/day_openers.json, shots/lines picked by "montage") + 25-35 s in-world scene with Chris/Martin, Lykta and the day's character + ONE quick-time moment (no fail state) + the TODAY'S THING card. Rows are data; the player is the /* dayscenes */ block. Source: build/dayscenes/make_data.py. Voices: voice/dayscene/<id>.m4a (placeholders; real ones in voice/dayscene/real/<id>.m4a + id in _real of durations.json). Wave 1 = days 3-10,14,16,20,22; wave 2 (story days) comes later.

3.title: Strike!

lines.t: Frame four! Did you see frame four?
I saw it. The whole street saw it. You did a dance.
It was a victory shuffle.
Boys. Something is moving in the woods again. It is probably a deer.
Probably.
Is it probably a deer, or is it probably-a-deer?
I have no data on the second kind.

qte.title: ROLL! Let go as the ring closes

say.t: Bowling is all timing. Let go as the ring closes.

ok.t: Strike. The pins fell over out of respect.

no.t: A gutter. A very graceful gutter. The pins did not even flinch.

lines.t: Today's thing: play one whole game at Bowlinghallen. Ten frames. It is warm in there.
Did the door just breathe?
Draught.

obj.head: STRIKE!
obj.text: Play one whole game at Bowlinghallen.
obj.sub: Rent a lane at the counter, then press G at a lane.

3.sign_note: A cold draught from the woods side; the shop door seems to breathe once.

4.title: Voices in the cold

lines.t: That was lovely. And then it stopped. Quite suddenly.
In tune, mostly. Why did they stop?
A broom came out of an upstairs window.
It had opinions about our key.
Whose broom?
We did not ask.
My grandfather said there is an eye on the hill. Old-timers always say that.
Which hill?
The one that looks back.

qte.title: Hold the candle steady. Let them finish the verse.

say.t: Hold the candle steady, Martin. The last verse needs a flame that does not bow.

ok.t: The flame stood up straight. The verse landed on its feet.

no.t: The flame bowed. The verse went home early, politely.

lines.t: The candles are all leaning the same way.
Candles do that. I have never looked into why.
Today's thing: go to the church and listen. They say they will try again.

obj.head: IN TUNE, MOSTLY
obj.text: Go to the church and listen to the carolers.

4.sign_note: Every candle flame leans the same way, toward the hill, once.

5.title: Pocket money

lines.t: There! A coin! ...It is a button.
A button.
A button of great promise.
The bank has not lost any coins. We counted. Twice.
Then whose are they?
The roads', apparently.
Ten is the unofficial target. I made that up. It sounds right.

say.t: Martin, the coin is rolling! Catch it, quick!

ok.t: Caught. It was a bottle cap. It counts, emotionally.

no.t: It rolled down a drain. It has gone to meet its family.

lines.t: Right. Ten coins. Let us go.
Right.
Today's thing: collect ten coins along the roads. They glow. Walk through them.

obj.head: COINS ON THE ROADS
obj.sub: Coins glow on the roads. Walk through them.

5.sign_note: The street lamp goes out for half a second and comes back. Nobody mentions it.

6.title: Tipi village

lines.t: Camp Botnan! Smoke straight up. That means a calm night.
Is that good?
The tipis are warm and the sky is not. Both are in the brochure.
Somebody is standing behind us. Far back, by the lamp.
Where?
It is... gone.
That will be Håkon. Or Per. Ask somebody else; I know everyone and I do not know that.

qte.title: Mash to rub your hands warm

say.t: It is very cold. Mash those hands together. Warm them up.

ok.t: Warm. Toasty. Your fingers have forgiven you.

no.t: Still cold. Ingrid hands over a spare mitten, tutting.

lines.t: Today's thing: visit Camp Botnan and look around the tipi village. It is up in the hills east of town.
Warm clothes.
And a friend who does not get followed.

obj.head: SMOKE STRAIGHT UP
obj.text: Visit Camp Botnan and look around the tipi village.
obj.sub: Up in the hills east of town.

6.sign_note: The colours drain for a moment while a still shape stands far down the street; it is gone with no footprints.

7.title: Mail from home

lines.t: Parcel for number three. It was open when it arrived.
Open how?
Mostly emptied. There is a note.
"Did you get the cookies? Six pepperkaker, in the blue tin. Love, Mum."
Six. We have not seen six.
We have not seen one.

qte.title: Shh. Hold still. Listen to the floor.

say.t: Shh. Do you hear that? Hold still and listen.

ok.t: Chewing. Wet, patient, enormous chewing. From the cellar window.

no.t: You sneezed. The chewing stopped. That is worse.

lines.t: Chris. Who lives downstairs?
A neighbour. Quiet. Likes sugar.
Today's thing: check the mailbox. It is right there. I will wait here; I have no hands.

obj.head: A LITTLE LIGHTER
obj.text: Check the mailbox at Chris's building.

7.sign_note: All the ambient sound drops out for a few seconds, leaving only the chewing under the floor.

8.title: Under the floorboards

lines.t: The ground-floor flat? Deeper than it looks.
Deeper how?
As deep as you make it.
That is not an answer.
No.
I would knock myself. But the floor has a sound under it now, and I have stopped.
And a smell. Old sugar.
Sugar.

qte.title: KNOCK on the ice as the ring closes

say.t: You want to know how deep it is? Knock on the ice. Politely.

ok.t: Tok. Tok. Tok. The ice answered in a deep, friendly voice. Then it stopped being friendly.

no.t: Tok. The ice said nothing. Then, very far down, it said something.

lines.t: Is it me, or is the fog coming up out of the ground?
It is the river.
The river is over there.
Today's thing: listen at the witch's flat. Quietly. And do not knock a fourth time.

obj.head: DEEPER THAN IT LOOKS
obj.text: Listen at the witch's flat. Find the trapdoor.

8.sign_note: A cold draught that seems to come up out of the ground; the fog thickens from below.

9.title: The big globe

lines.t: Another one from your mum.
A card. A recipe card. "Ginger, syrup, butter, flour. Baked with the first candle."
The first candle?
She always says that. I thought it was a joke.
A candle is a small fire that somebody agreed to. That is my whole professional opinion.
Crumbs. A trail of crumbs, up the hill.
Gingerbread. Big ones.
Too big for crumbs. These are crumbs of something bigger.

qte.title: Hold still. Look closely at the crumb.

say.t: Look closely. Hold still and let your eyes adjust.

ok.t: Ginger. Syrup. And one enormous tooth mark, politely rounded.

no.t: A crow got there first. The crow is not sorry.

lines.t: The birds just stopped.
They do that.
Today's thing: find Globen, the big globe on the hill. The crumbs go that way.

obj.head: GLOBEN
obj.sub: Follow the path past the tipi village.

9.sign_note: The birds stop for a few seconds, then start again, a little out of tune.

10.title: Top of the rock

lines.t: Another letter from Mum. It was open.
And chewed.
Mostly eaten. A stamp and half a sentence.
"...hope you are keeping warm and..." And that is all. The rest is gone.
Good morning.
Good morning, boys. Lovely coat, isn't it?
It is very big.
It is the coat. I wear it large.

qte.title: DUCK behind the mailbox! Tap now

say.t: She is turning around. Duck! Now!

ok.t: Ducked. She admired the mailbox for a long time.

no.t: She looked right at you and waved. Very warmly. Very hungrily.

lines.t: Today's thing: climb Orresteinen, the giant rock above the fjord. It is far. A car helps. Or a jetpack.
Why are we leaving?
Because I would like to be somewhere with fewer coats.

obj.head: THE LONG WAY DOWN
obj.sub: It is far. A car helps. Or a jetpack.

10.sign_note: A cold draught as the neighbour steps out, as if the door behind her is open onto somewhere much bigger.

14.title: Light the lights

lines.t: Every shop has its lights on. Except the tree.
Tonight is the night!
Start at the tree. Then one street at a time.
The cinema, the bank, the arcade and the Julerennet are all open today. The town has decided to be pleased.
We have decided to be pleased very carefully.

qte.title: Mash to crank the old generator

say.t: The tree's old generator needs cranking. Mash!

ok.t: Lit! Every bulb on the square said hello at once.

no.t: A cough of light, then a lovely wobbly glow. Good enough.

lines.t: Who lit that one? The little window over there.
Not me.
Not me.
A timer.
...A timer. Yes. Today's thing: walk the town and light the lights, starting at the tree.

obj.head: A LIGHT NOBODY LIT
obj.text: Walk the town and light the lights, starting at the tree.
obj.sub: The cinema, the arcade and the Julerennet are open too.

14.sign_note: One small window lights itself across the square. A timer, everybody agrees, a little too quickly.

16.title: The last parcel

lines.t: The mountain road is closed. There is a fence. Yesterday there was no fence.
A new fence. Very proud of itself.
The official line is: nothing to worry about. Please stay away.
Move along, please. Nothing to see.
We are not looking.
Looking is the first step.

qte.title: Hold still. Be a fence post.

say.t: A black car is slowing down. Hold still. Be a fence post.

ok.t: It rolled on. Probably lost. Probably.

no.t: It stopped. A window slid down one inch, then up again.

lines.t: Mum's last parcel is at the mailbox.
It smells of ginger, and a little of smoke. Today's thing: check the mailbox. Away from the fence.

obj.head: STAY AWAY
obj.text: Check the mailbox: the last parcel from Mum.

16.sign_note: The colours go cold and grey when the man in the black coat steps into view, like a door opening onto winter.

20.title: The crater
20.place: the frozen river, looking at the mountain

lines.t: Do you hear it?
No.
Exactly. No birds. No dogs. No wind.
My dog will not leave the cellar. She looks at the mountain, then at me.
Dogs know things.
She has never looked at me like that.

qte.title: Hold your breath. Be very quiet.

say.t: Be ready for quiet. Hold your breath. Hold it.

ok.t: Nothing noticed you. Nothing. You tell yourself that.

no.t: You breathed out. Far away, very slowly, something turned its head.

lines.t: I do not like slow things that do not stop.
Today's thing: go and look at the crater. Then run.

obj.head: BE READY FOR QUIET
obj.text: Go and look at the crater.
obj.sub: Stay on the flank. Then run.

20.sign_note: The sound drops out completely and the ground gives a very slow, very low tremor.

22.title: Slightly embarrassed lights

lines.t: The lights are back.
Some of them are embarrassed.
They are. Look at the third one. It is trying to hide behind the tree.
The case is closed. We have the answer.
What was the question?
That is not how it works.
Is the answer right?
The police are sure.

say.t: Someone is waving from a window. Wave back before they lose their nerve!

ok.t: Waved. They beamed. Somewhere a kettle went on.

no.t: A late wave. Awkward. Still warm, though. Still counts.

lines.t: Warm is a team sport. Today's thing: check on a neighbour, starting with the flat next door.
Next door is the lady with the cookies.
Good. I hope there are cookies.

obj.head: SLIGHTLY EMBARRASSED LIGHTS
obj.text: Check on a neighbour, starting with the flat next door.
obj.sub: Coins can wait. Bring a few for the cafe if you like.

22.sign_note: A few of the lamps flick on and off sheepishly, like a bad joke told twice.

lines.t: Chris! Martin! You came! Look at you, standing in my square.
I am the mayor. Everything is perfect. Absolutely perfect. Welcome to downtown!
Um. The tree just went dark.
Resting! The lights are resting. They worked so hard all November.
Where is everybody? The street is empty.
Exactly where they should be. Indoors. Nobody is hiding. That would be weird, and nothing weird ever happens here.
Mayor, my sensors report a great deal of quiet.
Peace and quiet! Lovely. We had a goose once. It was fine.
A woman on a broom just wrecked all the decorations.
Wind! Lovely, hat-wearing wind. We get it every year.
The tree lot is open. Pick a nice one and go home before it gets late. Not because of anything.
I will be right here. I am always right here. Smile!
